whatFailed: The scenario's setup call, POST /v2/bookings sent with the header value the published Cal.com docs mandate (cal-api-version: 2026-02-25), returned 400 instead of 201, because the tested Cal.diy build does not implement a 2026-02-25 API version and silently downgraded the request to the 2024-04-15 booking controller, whose input contract is completely different.

docClaim.quote: operationId: BookingsController_2026_02_25_createBooking / parameters: - name: cal-api-version, in: header, description: 'Must be set to 2026-02-25.', required: true, schema: {type: string, example: '2026-02-25', default: '2026-02-25'}. The same page warns: "Please make sure to pass in the cal-api-version header value as mentioned in the Headers section. Not passing the correct value will default to an older version of this endpoint." Two body fields on that page are further marked "Only supported on the 2026-02-25 API version" (allowBookingOutOfBounds, skipBookingLimits).
docClaim.section: create-a-booking/openapi (POST /v2/bookings, cal-api-version header). The scenario itself binds to .truecourse/specs/sources/cal.com-docs/docs/api-reference/v2/bookings-attendees/add-an-attendee-to-a-booking.md, which correctly prescribes cal-api-version: 2024-08-13 and is NOT the page that failed.

observed: POST /v2/bookings with Cal-Api-Version: 2026-02-25 and body {start, attendee:{name,timeZone,email}, eventTypeId:100} answered 400 with three validation errors on top-level properties the documented body does not even contain: timeZone (isTimeZone), language (isString), metadata (isObject). The error target echoes back only {start, eventTypeId}: the documented attendee object was stripped before validation. The server boot log in server.stdout.txt shows POST /v2/bookings is mapped only for versions 2024-04-15, 2024-06-11, 2024-06-14 and 2024-08-13; no 2026-02-25 route exists. Steps 2 to 6, which carry all 11 add-attendee milestones, never ran.
impact: Any self-hoster who follows the current published Cal.com create-a-booking reference verbatim cannot create a booking: the mandated header value is unknown to the open-source build, the request is silently routed to the 2024-04-15 handler, and the 400 blames three fields that appear nowhere in the documented request body. 22 of the 101 scenarios in this run died on exactly this response. For this scenario specifically the add-attendee contract itself was left unverified.

rootCause.explanation: The Cal.diy API version registry tops out at 2024-09-04 (VERSION_2024_06_14, VERSION_2024_06_11, VERSION_2024_04_15, VERSION_2024_08_13, VERSION_2024_09_04 collected into API_VERSIONS). There is no 2026-02-25 constant, no BookingsController_2026_02_25, and no allowBookingOutOfBounds / skipBookingLimits field anywhere in the tested worktree (verified by full-tree grep for '2026-02-25' and '2026_02_25', zero hits, and by 'grep -rn "export class BookingsController" apps/api/v2/src', which returns only BookingsController_2024_08_13 and BookingsController_2024_04_15). The failure mode is produced by apps/api/v2/src/bootstrap.ts lines 31-41: the custom NestJS version extractor returns the header value only when API_VERSIONS.includes(headerVersion), and otherwise returns VERSION_2024_04_15, with defaultVersion also VERSION_2024_04_15. So an unrecognized value is not rejected, it is silently downgraded to the OLDEST handler. That handler validates against CreateBookingInput_2024_04_15 (apps/api/v2/src/platform/bookings/2024-04-15/inputs/create-booking.input.ts lines 122-146), where timeZone is @IsTimeZone(), language is @IsString() and metadata is @IsObject(), all non-optional, which is exactly the three-error payload observed. The global ValidationPipe in bootstrap.ts line 60 runs with whitelist: true, which is why the documented 'attendee' object was stripped from the error target. The decisive edition evidence is inside the tested worktree itself: docs/api-reference/v2/openapi.json is git-tracked (last touched by ab21c7f805 'refactor: Cal.diy' (#28903), 2026-04-15), is titled 'Cal.diy API v2', and declares POST /v2/bookings as operationId BookingsController_2024_08_13_createBooking with cal-api-version default '2024-08-13'. The published Cal.com page for the same route declares BookingsController_2026_02_25_createBooking with default '2026-02-25'. The two editions genuinely serve different newest handlers for this endpoint. By contrast the bound add-attendee page matches Cal.diy exactly: the repo's own openapi.json declares BookingAttendeesController_2024_08_13_addAttendee with the same BookingAttendeeOutput_2024_08_13 schema (name, email, displayEmail, timeZone, language, absent, phoneNumber, id, bookingId), so nothing about the endpoint under test is edition-divergent.

introducedBy.title: feat: API v2 subversioning
introducedBy.note: This is the commit that introduced the silent-downgrade extractor (VersioningType.CUSTOM with 'return VERSION_2024_04_15' as the fallback for any unrecognized cal-api-version), verified with 'git show 3a22fdb42 -- apps/api/v2/src/app.ts'. Blame on the tested worktree attributes bootstrap.ts lines 31-41 to 9ad8aa981ac (2026-01-13, #26735 'chore: deploy api v2 on vercel'), but that commit only moved the block; 'git log -L 31,41:apps/api/v2/src/bootstrap.ts' walks back through 56b29b5df6 (2026-01-09, #26604, rename app.ts to bootstrap.ts) to 0a15483c46 (2024-03-20, #14106) where versioning was still URI-based, so #15135 is the real origin. The edition divergence itself has NO commit in this repo: the version registry packages/platform/constants/api.ts was last touched by dcf10935de (2026-01-07, #25739) and still stops at 2024-09-04, while 2026-02-25 was added on the closed hosted side. Old code, newer interaction: the fallback is from 2024, the harm comes from the 2026 docs pointing at a version the open-source build never received.

fixedAfter.note: in cal.diy: no. Only 4 commits landed between the tested 038381aeca and origin/main 176037d0af (2026-08-08): #29940 emails, #29901 language update, #29740 phone-input country fallback, #29819 Clara app. 'git log 038381aeca..origin/main' over apps/api/v2/src/bootstrap.ts, apps/api/v2/src/lib/api-versions.ts, packages/platform/constants/api.ts, apps/api/v2/src/platform/bookings and packages/platform/types/bookings returns nothing, and a full-tree grep for 2026-02-25 on main is still empty, so main still tops out at 2024-08-13 and still downgrades unknown versions silently. in cal.com: cannot be checked in source, and the brief's cross-reference clone is not what it claims to be. 'gh api repos/calcom/cal.com' returns full_name calcom/cal.diy (repo created 2021-03-22, default branch main): the original calcom/cal.com repository was RENAMED to calcom/cal.diy, so github.com/calcom/cal.com now redirects there. That is why <scratch>/src/calcom and <scratch>/src/caldiy sit on the identical HEAD 176037d0afbe572f870a3c702985e7cd83fe6c0c and contain byte-identical apps/api/v2 trees. There is no public commercial cal.com source to point at. The only proof that hosted Cal.com serves 2026-02-25 is its published OpenAPI, whose operationId is BookingsController_2026_02_25_createBooking. Direction of travel is divergence, not convergence: the hosted product moved to a newer booking handler and the open-source build did not receive it.

notes:
Two things a maintainer and the doc author should each take away, and one thing the guard corpus should fix.

1. For the doc author: cal.com/docs/api-reference/v2/bookings/create-a-booking is generated from the hosted OpenAPI and is the only reference a self-hoster finds. It tells every reader to send cal-api-version: 2026-02-25 and marks it required with that default. Self-hosted Cal.diy has never had that version. The page should either state the version floor for self-hosted builds or the self-hosted docs should be published from the repo's own docs/api-reference/v2/openapi.json, which already says 2024-08-13 and is correct.

2. For the maintainer: the silent downgrade in apps/api/v2/src/bootstrap.ts lines 31-41 is what turns a version mismatch into an unreadable bug report. An unrecognized cal-api-version should answer 400 or 404 naming the supported versions rather than falling through to the 2024-04-15 handler and emitting constraint errors for timeZone, language and metadata, three fields that do not exist in the request the caller actually sent. Open issue #23136 is a user hitting exactly this and getting no answer for a year. Note the fallback itself IS documented ("Not passing the correct value will default to an older version of this endpoint"), which is precisely why this is an edition mismatch rather than a code defect: the product does what its docs say it does when the version is not recognized; the only gap is that the docs' 'correct value' is not correct in this edition.

3. For the guard corpus: the failing step is an UNBOUND precondition (note: "Prepares the existing booking the attendee is added TO"), not an assertion. It carries no milestone, and the page it binds to says nothing about 2026-02-25. The sibling scenario read-the-attendees-of-a-booking.api.1 issues the same create with the same body shape under cal-api-version: 2024-08-13 and PASSES, as does the-caller-must-be-permitted-to-add-an-attendee.api.1, so the generator is inconsistent about which version it pins preconditions to. Because step 1 died, all 11 add-attendee milestones (route, envelope, seven required output fields, displayEmail, phoneNumber echo, language enum, body-required, email-required, locale-refusal, list-membership) went unverified. Regenerating step 1 with cal-api-version: 2024-08-13 would let this scenario actually test its subject, and the 2026-02-25 claim should live in its own dedicated version scenario, which the corpus already does elsewhere: reassign-a-round-robin-booking.api.1 carries a step whose note reads "the page states the header is required and must be 2026-02-25 ... (transform-gaps D1 - this checkout serves 2024-08-13)", so the pipeline already knew about the gap.

4. Forward-looking caution for whoever re-runs this: seated-bookings-refuse-attendees-and-guests.api.1 got a real 201 from POST /v2/bookings/{uid}/attendees whose body was {name, email, displayEmail, timeZone, language, absent, id, bookingId} with NO phoneNumber key (it did not send one). Step 2 of this scenario asserts data.phoneNumber equals '+19876543210'. That assertion is untested here and could well be the next failure; it is not evidence of anything yet.

5. Cross-batch correction: <scratch>/src/calcom is not the commercial Cal.com repository. github.com/calcom/cal.com redirects to calcom/cal.diy (the repo was renamed), so that clone is a second copy of cal.diy at the same HEAD. Any Cal.diy verdict in this batch that relies on "the code exists in calcom/cal.com main" as edition-mismatch evidence cannot be satisfied that way, and "fixed in cal.com" cannot be checked from source at all.
